schemeDescription: Central sector scheme providing income support to all landholding farmer families across the country.
objective: To supplement financial needs of farmers for procuring inputs related to agriculture and allied activities.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
eligibilityCriteria: All landholding farmer families (subject to certain exclusion criteria like institutional landholders, income tax payers, government employees above certain grade, professionals).
benefits: Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 each, transferred directly to bank accounts.
applicationProcess: Register online via PM-KISAN portal or through Common Service Centres (CSC) / local revenue/agriculture officer with land records.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, land ownership documents, bank account passbook, citizenship certificate
beneficiaries: Approx. 9.4 crore landholding farmer families (as of the 23rd installment, June 2026)
annualBenefit: Rs. 6,000 per year per farmer family, paid in 3 installments of Rs. 2,000 each

schemeName: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
schemeDescription: World's largest health assurance scheme providing free health cover for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
objective: To provide health insurance cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year to economically vulnerable families.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
state: All India (Central Scheme, state implementation varies)
eligibilityCriteria: Families identified as deprived/occupational category as per Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data; automatic inclusion/exclusion criteria apply.
benefits: Cashless and paperless health cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization at empanelled hospitals.
applicationProcess: Check eligibility online, visit nearest Ayushman Bharat Kendra/CSC or empanelled hospital's Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra desk to get Ayushman card made.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, ration card, SECC 2011 verification, mobile number
beneficiaries: Over 12 crore poor and vulnerable families (approx. 55 crore individuals) eligible; over 12.6 crore hospital admissions authorised as of June 2026
annualBenefit: Health cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization

schemeDescription: Housing scheme aimed at providing pucca houses to urban poor and economically weaker sections.
objective: To achieve 'Housing for All' by providing affordable housing to eligible urban households.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
eligibilityCriteria: EWS/LIG/MIG households without a pucca house anywhere in India; income-based categorization (EWS up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG up to Rs 6 lakh, MIG up to Rs 18 lakh annual income).
benefits: Interest subsidy on home loans under Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme, direct financial assistance for construction (varies by component: BLC, AHP, ISSR, CLSS).
applicationProcess: Apply online through PMAY-U portal or through Common Service Centres / Urban Local Bodies.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, income certificate, bank account details, property documents, photograph
beneficiaries: Over 1.22 crore houses sanctioned since 2015, of which over 97 lakh completed (as of Feb 2026, including PMAY-U 2.0)
annualBenefit: Central assistance up to Rs. 1.5-2.5 lakh per house or interest subsidy on home loans, depending on the component

schemeDescription: Rural housing scheme to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to rural poor.
objective: To provide financial assistance for construction of pucca houses to houseless and those living in kutcha/dilapidated houses in rural areas.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Rural Development
state: All India (Rural areas, Centrally Sponsored Scheme)
eligibilityCriteria: Houseless households and households living in kutcha/dilapidated houses as per SECC 2011 / Awaas+ data.
benefits: Financial assistance of Rs. 1.20 lakh (plain areas) / Rs. 1.30 lakh (hilly/difficult areas) for house construction, plus support for toilet under Swachh Bharat Mission.
applicationProcess: Beneficiaries identified through SECC/Awaas+ survey; verification done by Gram Sabha; apply/track via PMAY-G portal.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, MGNREGA job card (if available), bank account, SECC data verification
beneficiaries: Approx. 3 crore rural houses completed as of March 2026, against an expanded target of 4.95 crore houses by 2029
annualBenefit: One-time assistance of Rs. 1.20 lakh (plain areas) or Rs. 1.30 lakh (hilly/NE areas) per house, plus MGNREGS labour support

schemeDescription: Scheme to provide LPG connections to women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.
objective: To safeguard the health of women and children by providing clean cooking fuel and reduce dependence on unclean fuels.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
eligibilityCriteria: Adult women from BPL/eligible households (SC/ST, PMAY beneficiaries, Antyodaya Anna Yojana, forest dwellers, most backward classes, etc.) who do not already have an LPG connection.
benefits: Free LPG gas connection with security deposit waiver, first refill and stove often subsidized/free in initial phase.
applicationProcess: Apply through nearest LPG distributor (Indane, Bharat Gas, HP Gas) with KYC form or apply online.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, BPL ration card/eligibility proof, bank account details, passport-size photograph
beneficiaries: Over 10 crore free LPG connections provided to BPL households since 2016
annualBenefit: One-time assistance of Rs. 1,600 per connection (cylinder security deposit + cylinder cost), plus subsidy on LPG refills

schemeName: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
schemeDescription: Employment guarantee scheme assuring at least 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households.
objective: To enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing guaranteed wage employment for unskilled manual work.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Rural Development
state: All India (Rural areas, Centrally Sponsored Scheme)
eligibilityCriteria: Adult members (18+ years) of rural households willing to do unskilled manual work.
benefits: Guaranteed 100 days of wage employment per financial year per household at notified minimum wage rates.
applicationProcess: Apply for a Job Card at the Gram Panchayat office; submit written/verbal application for work; work provided within 15 days.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, residence proof, photograph (for Job Card)
beneficiaries: Over 26 crore registered workers nationally, with roughly 10-11 crore active workers engaging in work annually
annualBenefit: Guaranteed 100 days of wage employment per household per year at notified minimum wage rates

schemeDescription: National financial inclusion mission to ensure access to banking, credit, insurance and pension for the unbanked.
objective: To provide universal access to banking facilities with at least one basic bank account for every household.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
eligibilityCriteria: Any Indian citizen without a bank account; age 10+ can open account.
benefits: Zero-balance bank account, RuPay debit card with accidental insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh, overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000, access to pension and insurance schemes.
applicationProcess: Visit nearest bank branch or Bank Mitra (Business Correspondent) with KYC documents to open account.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card or any valid ID/address proof, photograph
beneficiaries: Over 55 crore bank accounts opened since 2014 (approx. 36-45 crore in rural/semi-urban areas)
annualBenefit: Zero-balance bank account with RuPay card carrying Rs. 2 lakh accidental insurance cover and overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000

schemeDescription: Government-backed pension scheme targeted at workers in the unorganized sector.
objective: To provide old age income security by encouraging people to save for pension through defined contributions.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services / Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
eligibilityCriteria: Indian citizens aged 18-40 years with a savings bank account/post office savings account.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 after age 60, depending on contribution amount and age of joining.
applicationProcess: Apply through the bank/post office where savings account is held, via net banking or physical form.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, savings bank account details, mobile number
beneficiaries: Over 7.5-9 crore cumulative enrolments as of 2025-26
annualBenefit: Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 after age 60, based on contribution amount

schemeName: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
schemeDescription: Government-backed life insurance scheme offering affordable life cover.
objective: To increase life insurance penetration among low-income and unorganized sector individuals.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
eligibilityCriteria: Individuals aged 18-50 years with a bank/post office account, who give consent for auto-debit.
benefits: Life insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh in case of death (any reason), for an annual premium of Rs. 436 (as per revised rates).
applicationProcess: Enroll through bank/post office where account is held, via auto-debit consent form, renewable annually.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, bank account details, nominee details
beneficiaries: Over 23 crore cumulative enrolments as of March 2025
annualBenefit: Life insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh for an annual premium of Rs. 436

schemeDescription: Government-backed accidental insurance scheme offering affordable accident cover.
objective: To provide accidental death and disability cover at a very low premium to promote financial inclusion.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
eligibilityCriteria: Individuals aged 18-70 years with a bank/post office account, who give consent for auto-debit.
benefits: Accidental death/full disability cover of Rs. 2 lakh and partial disability cover of Rs. 1 lakh, for an annual premium of Rs. 20 (as per revised rates).
applicationProcess: Enroll through bank/post office where account is held, via auto-debit consent form, renewable annually.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, bank account details, nominee details
beneficiaries: Over 50-58 crore cumulative enrolments as of 2025-26
annualBenefit: Accidental death/disability cover of Rs. 2 lakh for an annual premium of Rs. 20

schemeDescription: National campaign to address declining child sex ratio and promote education and welfare of the girl child.
objective: To prevent gender-biased sex selective elimination, ensure survival & protection of the girl child and her education.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Women and Child Development
eligibilityCriteria: Focused on families with girl children, particularly in districts with low child sex ratio.
educationCriteria: Aims to ensure enrollment and retention of girl children in schools
benefits: Awareness generation, multi-sectoral interventions, incentives linked to schemes like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana for girl child welfare.
applicationProcess: Implemented through district-level task forces, Anganwadi centres, and schools; no individual application required for the core scheme.
requiredDocuments: Birth certificate of girl child, Aadhaar card (for linked benefit schemes)
beneficiaries: Nationwide campaign covering all districts in India, with focused interventions in districts with low child sex ratio
annualBenefit: Not a direct cash-benefit scheme; provides awareness generation and multi-sectoral interventions for the girl child

schemeDescription: Small savings scheme for the girl child under the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative.
objective: To encourage parents to build a fund for the future education and marriage expenses of their girl child.
ministryDepartment: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance / Department of Posts
eligibilityCriteria: Girl child below the age of 10 years; account can be opened by parents/legal guardian; maximum two accounts per family (with exceptions for twins/triplets).
benefits: High interest rate (revised quarterly by government), tax benefits under Section 80C, maturity after 21 years or on marriage of girl after 18 years.
applicationProcess: Open account at any post office or authorized bank branch with initial deposit (minimum Rs. 250).
requiredDocuments: Girl child's birth certificate, identity/address proof of guardian, photographs
beneficiaries: Over 4.53 crore girl child accounts opened, with total deposits exceeding Rs. 3.33 lakh crore (as of December 2025)
annualBenefit: Minimum deposit Rs. 250, maximum Rs. 1.5 lakh per year; interest rate of 8.2% p.a. (tax-free under Section 80C)

schemeDescription: Scheme to facilitate bank loans for greenfield enterprises set up by SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.
objective: To promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities by facilitating bank loans.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
eligibilityCriteria: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs above 18 years setting up a greenfield (first-time) enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or allied agriculture.
benefits: Bank loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore for setting up new enterprises, covering 75% of the project cost.
applicationProcess: Apply online via Stand-Up India portal or approach nearest bank branch directly.
requiredDocuments: Identity/address proof, caste certificate (for SC/ST), business project report, bank account details
beneficiaries: Over 2.5-3 lakh accounts (loans) sanctioned to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs since 2016, with about 80% going to women
annualBenefit: One-time bank loan between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore per beneficiary for a greenfield enterprise

schemeDescription: Credit-linked subsidy scheme for generating self-employment through establishment of micro-enterprises.
objective: To generate employment opportunities in rural and urban areas through setting up of new self-employment ventures/projects/micro-enterprises.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
eligibilityCriteria: Individuals above 18 years; for projects above Rs. 10 lakh (manufacturing) / Rs. 5 lakh (service), minimum VIII standard pass required.
educationCriteria: Minimum Class VIII pass required for projects above specified cost limits; no minimum education for smaller projects
benefits: Margin money subsidy of 15-35% of project cost (higher for special categories/rural areas), maximum project cost Rs. 50 lakh (manufacturing) / Rs. 20 lakh (service).
applicationProcess: Apply online through the PMEGP e-portal (KVIC), with project report and required documents.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, educational qualification certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), project report, passport photo
beneficiaries: Several lakh micro-enterprises assisted since inception, generating employment for lakhs of individuals annually
annualBenefit: Margin money subsidy of 15-35% of project cost, up to Rs. 50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs. 20 lakh (service) per unit

schemeDescription: Scheme providing collateral-free loans to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
objective: To provide funding to small business owners and entrepreneurs in the non-corporate small business sector.
ministryDepartment: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
eligibilityCriteria: Any Indian citizen with a business plan for a non-farm income generating activity in manufacturing, trading or services with credit need up to Rs. 20 lakh.
benefits: Collateral-free loans under three categories: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishor (Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakh), Tarun (Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (up to Rs. 20 lakh).
applicationProcess: Apply at nearest bank branch, NBFC or MFI, or online via the Udyamimitra/Jan Samarth portal.
requiredDocuments: Identity/address proof, business plan, bank account details, passport photo
beneficiaries: Over 52-59 crore loans sanctioned since 2015, amounting to over Rs. 33-41 lakh crore (as of 2025-26)
annualBenefit: Collateral-free loans up to Rs. 20 lakh under Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories

schemeDescription: Flagship skill development scheme providing free short-term skill training and certification.
objective: To enable Indian youth to take up industry-relevant skill training for better livelihood opportunities.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
eligibilityCriteria: Indian citizens, primarily unemployed youth and school/college dropouts; age criteria vary by training scheme component.
educationCriteria: No fixed minimum education requirement; varies by trade/job role
benefits: Free skill training aligned to National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF), certification, and monetary reward on successful assessment.
applicationProcess: Register at nearest PMKVY training centre or apply online through the Skill India portal.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, educational certificates, bank account details, photograph
beneficiaries: Over 1.4 crore candidates trained across PMKVY 1.0 and 2.0 phases since 2015
annualBenefit: Free skill training and certification, plus a monetary reward on successful assessment

schemeDescription: Crop insurance scheme providing financial support to farmers in case of crop failure due to natural calamities.
objective: To provide comprehensive insurance coverage against crop failure to stabilize farmers' income.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
state: All India (Centrally Sponsored Scheme, voluntary for states)
eligibilityCriteria: All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas.
benefits: Insurance coverage and financial support for crop loss due to natural calamities, pests and diseases; low premium (2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops).
applicationProcess: Apply through banks (for loanee farmers, often automatic), Common Service Centres, insurance company agents, or the National Crop Insurance Portal.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, land records, bank account details, sowing certificate
beneficiaries: Over 4 crore farmers enrolled in 2024-25 alone; nearly 78.7 crore cumulative farmer applications insured since 2016
annualBenefit: Crop insurance coverage with farmer premium capped at 1.5-5% of sum insured, depending on the crop season

schemeName: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
schemeDescription: Micro-credit scheme for street vendors to help them resume livelihoods affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
objective: To provide affordable working capital loans to street vendors to restart their businesses.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
eligibilityCriteria: Street vendors in possession of Certificate of Vending/Identity Card issued by Urban Local Bodies, or identified in the survey.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loan up to Rs. 10,000 (first tranche), with subsequent higher loans of Rs. 20,000 and Rs. 50,000 on timely repayment, plus interest subsidy and cashback on digital transactions.
applicationProcess: Apply online through the PM SVANidhi portal or through Urban Local Bodies/lending institutions.
requiredDocuments: Certificate of Vending/Identity Card, Aadhaar card, bank account details
beneficiaries: Over 75 lakh street vendors benefited, with over 1.1 crore loans disbursed worth about Rs. 17,800 crore (as of 2026)
annualBenefit: Working capital loans of Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 50,000 (progressively higher on repayment), plus 7% interest subsidy and digital cashback

schemeDescription: Common platform for various central and state government scholarship schemes for students.
objective: To provide financial assistance to students from underprivileged/minority/economically weaker backgrounds for pursuing education.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (platform) / Multiple Ministries (individual schemes)
eligibilityCriteria: Varies by scheme; generally based on family income, category (SC/ST/OBC/Minority), and academic performance.
educationCriteria: Student enrolled in a recognized school/college/university, ranging from Class I to postgraduate/PhD level depending on the specific scheme.
benefits: Financial assistance covering tuition fees, maintenance allowance, and other educational expenses, varying by scheme.
applicationProcess: Register and apply online on the National Scholarship Portal with institution verification.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, income certificate, caste/category certificate, bank account details, previous academic mark sheets, bonafide certificate from institution
beneficiaries: Several crore students benefit annually across the various scholarship schemes hosted on the portal
annualBenefit: Varies by scheme; covers tuition fees and maintenance allowance for eligible students

schemeDescription: Scheme to provide end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople working with hands and tools.
objective: To improve the quality and reach of products and services of artisans and craftspeople, integrating them with domestic and global value chains.
ministryDepartment: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
eligibilityCriteria: Artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 identified trades, working through hands and tools, registered via Common Service Centres.
benefits: Recognition through PM Vishwakarma certificate/ID card, skill training with stipend, toolkit incentive up to Rs. 15,000, collateral-free credit up to Rs. 3 lakh in two tranches at concessional interest rate.
applicationProcess: Register through Common Service Centre (CSC) with biometric authentication; verification by ULB/Gram Panchayat.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar card, bank account details, trade-related proof
beneficiaries: Around 30 lakh artisans/craftspeople registered, of which about 23 lakh have been trained (as of December 2025)
annualBenefit: Toolkit incentive up to Rs. 15,000 and collateral-free credit up to Rs. 3 lakh in two tranches at concessional interest rates
